preconditions.description: Attacker must hold some NOMOS tokens to initiate transfer
Contract must have accumulated ETH balance from previous token swaps (swapAndLiquify must have been triggered)

violation_target.exploit_hint: The contract has a reentrancy vulnerability in the swapAndLiquify function due to unsafe external calls. Create a malicious contract that implements a fallback/receive function. When swapAndLiquify is triggered (by selling tokens to the pair), the contract will call addLiquidity which makes an external ETH transfer via uniswapV2Router.addLiquidityETH. The attacker's contract can re-enter during the ETH transfer and call swapAndLiquify again before state updates, potentially draining ETH from the contract. The attack requires: 1) Deploy malicious contract with reentrant fallback, 2) Trigger swapAndLiquify by selling tokens to uniswapV2Pair when contract has accumulated enough tokens, 3) Re-enter during addLiquidity to exploit the reentrancy.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has a classic reentrancy vulnerability in the swapAndLiquify function. The function calls addLiquidity which makes an external call to uniswapV2Router.addLiquidityETH with ETH value. This external call can be intercepted by a malicious contract with a receive() function. The inSwapAndLiquify flag is set via lockTheSwap modifier, but the reentrancy can happen during the external router call before state updates are completed. The attacker can re-enter swapAndLiquify multiple times to drain ETH from the contract.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Deploy a malicious contract that implements a receive() function to re-enter swapAndLiquify. 2. Ensure the target contract has accumulated enough tokens to trigger swapAndLiquify (minimumTokensBeforeSwap). 3. Trigger swapAndLiquify by selling tokens to the pair. 4. During the ETH transfer in addLiquidity, re-enter swapAndLiquify to drain more ETH before state updates.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Create a malicious contract with receive() function that calls swapAndLiquify again. 2. Get some NOMOS tokens to initiate the attack. 3. Ensure swapAndLiquifyEnabled is true (default is false, so we may need to enable it via owner). 4. Accumulate tokens in the contract by making transfers that trigger fees. 5. Trigger swapAndLiquify by selling tokens to the pair. 6. During reentrancy, drain ETH from the contract.
